# Read in data

Please run 01-Data_Cleaning_FAIR_Retrospective first

```{r}
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
alex_doi_new1 <- read_csv("output_data/alex_doi_new1.csv")
```

# Country Code analysis

This code chunk is redundant if you ran 01-Data_Cleaning_FAIR_Retrospective.R recently and it is still cached in memory.

```{r}
#### Country Codes ####
# code modified from google ai search on July 1, 2026
# pivot the data frame longer
country_wide <- alex_doi_new1 %>%
  select(.row_id, authorships.countries) %>%
  # separate multiple rows
  separate_rows(authorships.countries, sep = "\\|") %>%
  mutate(
    country = str_trim(authorships.countries),
    country = toupper(country),         
    country = na_if(country, "")        # drop NA's
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country)) %>%
  distinct(.row_id, country) %>%        
  mutate(has_country = 1L) %>%          
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = country,
    values_from = has_country,
    values_fill = 0
  )

library(countrycode)
# create a country code dictionary
country_codes <- names(country_wide)

# remove non‑country columns like ".row_id"
country_codes <- country_codes[country_codes != ".row_id"]

# create a country code dictionary using  ISO‑3166‑1 country code 
country_dict <- data.frame(
  code = country_codes,
  country = countrycode(country_codes, origin = "iso2c", destination = "country.name")
)

country_dict$country[country_dict$code == "XK"] <- "Kosovo" # add Kosovo

# Join back to original if you want the rest of the columns:
alex_doi_new_wide <- alex_doi_new1 %>%
  left_join(country_wide, by = ".row_id") %>%
  select(-.row_id)

```

OPTIONAL

```{r}
# write to csv
write.csv(alex_doi_new_wide, file = "output_data/alex_doi_new_wide.csv")

```

# Summary Chart of DOI

Simple Summary Chart for the Numbers of DOI in the Domain, Field, and Subfield

```{r}
# Summary table grouped by the unique DOI
domain_summary <- alex_doi_new1 %>%
  filter(Domain !="") %>%
  group_by(Domain) %>%
  summarise(
    unique_dois_count = n_distinct(doi, na.rm = TRUE),
    unique_field_count = n_distinct(Field, na.rm = TRUE),
    unique_subfield_count = n_distinct(Subfield, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Print the resulting table
print(domain_summary)

```

# Field Tables

```{r}
# generate a table with count of the top Field
# Read the Google AI summary on how to add numbers for top field on 8/31 
field_table <- alex_doi_new1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(doi)) %>%
  mutate(
    Domain = coalesce(Domain, "Unclassified"),
    Field  = coalesce(Field,  "Unclassified")
  ) %>%
  group_by(Domain, Field) %>%
  summarise(doi_count = n_distinct(doi), .groups = "drop")

field_table <- field_table %>%
  group_by(Domain) %>%
  mutate(
    is_top_field = doi_count == max(doi_count),
    label_text = if_else(
      is_top_field,
      paste0(Field, "\n(n = ", doi_count, ")"),
      Field
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

# Treemap graphic using the Okabe Ito color scheme

```{r}
okabe_ito <- c("#009E73", "#F0E442", "#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#0072B2") 

library(showtext)
font_add(family = "Arial", regular = "Arial.ttf")
showtext_auto()

```

With a horizontal legend. Used Claude Sonnet 5.5 Medium on 9/28/26 to move the legend to horizontal.

```{r}
library(forcats)

field_table <- field_table %>%
  mutate(Domain = fct_reorder(Domain, doi_count, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE))

domain_order <- field_table %>%
  group_by(Domain) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(doi_count)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total)) %>%
  pull(Domain)

field_table$Domain <- factor(field_table$Domain, levels = domain_order)

library(treemapify)
ggplot(field_table, aes(area = doi_count, fill = Domain, label = label_text, subgroup = Domain)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text(colour = "black", place = "center", reflow = TRUE, size = 14,
                    family = "Arial", min.size = 5) +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border(colour = "darkgrey", size = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = okabe_ito) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Publications by Domain and Field") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )

```

# Table of countries

## list of countries

Logic for the countries count. Generated with the assistance of Google ai mode on July 1 2026. Run 01-Data_Cleaning_FAIR first to create the list of countries

```{r}
DATE_MIN   <- as.Date("2016-03-15")
DATE_MAX   <- as.Date("2026-03-15")

code_col <- intersect(c("code", "iso2", "iso2c", "country_code"), names(country_dict))
name_col <- intersect(c("name", "country_name", "country", "label"),  names(country_dict))

if (length(code_col) == 0) stop("country_dict must have a code column.")
country_dict_std <- if (length(name_col) == 0) {
  country_dict %>% rename(code = !!code_col[1]) %>% mutate(name = code)
} else {
  country_dict %>% rename(code = !!code_col[1], name = !!name_col[1])
}

country_codes <- names(alex_doi_new_wide)[str_detect(names(alex_doi_new_wide), "^[A-Z]{2}$")]
```

```{r}
df_long <- alex_doi_new_wide %>%
  filter(publication_date >= DATE_MIN, publication_date <= DATE_MAX) %>%
  mutate(publication_year = as.integer(publication_year)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(publication_year), publication_year > 2015) %>%
  select(publication_year, doi_clean, all_of(country_codes)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(country_codes),
               names_to = "country_code", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(!is.na(value), value > 0) %>%
  left_join(country_dict_std, by = c("country_code" = "code")) %>%
  mutate(country_name = coalesce(name, country_code)) %>%
  select(publication_year, doi_clean, country_code, country_name, value)

summary_full <- df_long %>%
  group_by(publication_year, country_code, country_name) %>%
  summarise(count = n_distinct(doi_clean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(publication_year) %>%
  mutate(year_total = sum(count)) %>%
  ungroup()

all_countries <- sort(unique(summary_full$country_name))

```

#### Finding the Subfields not represented

We have coverage in all domains and fields. and 214 out of 252 subfields in OpenAlex. claude.ai prompt for Sonnet 5 Medium on Aug. 24, 2026 - I asked create a API pull in OpenAlex using R to get subfields data. There are 252 subfields. The Subfields endpoint is at `api.openalex.org/subfields`. What are they? I modified the response code to...

```{r}
library(httr2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

subfields_df <- request("https://api.openalex.org/subfields") %>%
  req_url_query(per_page = 200) %>%
  req_perform() %>%
  resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE) %>%
  .$results %>%
  transmute(
    subfield_id    = id,
    subfield_name  = display_name,
    field_id       = field$id,
    field_name     = field$display_name,
    domain_id      = domain$id,
    domain_name    = domain$display_name,
    works_count,
    cited_by_count
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_id"), ~ sub(".*/", "", .x))) %>%
  arrange(domain_name, field_name, subfield_name)
```

```{r}
get_page <- function(p) {
  request("https://api.openalex.org/subfields") %>%
    req_url_query(per_page = 200, page = p) %>%
    req_perform() %>%
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE) %>%
    .$results
}

subfields_df <- bind_rows(get_page(1), get_page(2)) %>%
  transmute(
    subfield_id    = id,
    subfield_name  = display_name,
    field_id       = field$id,
    field_name     = field$display_name,
    domain_id      = domain$id,
    domain_name    = domain$display_name,
    works_count,
    cited_by_count
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_id"), ~ sub(".*/", "", .x))) %>%
  arrange(domain_name, field_name, subfield_name)

nrow(subfields_df)   # should be 252
```

Google prompt "can you compare two variables in two different datasets" on 8/24/2026

Google AI Mode. dataframe A and dataframe b compare the different responses in the same columns (column names are slightly different) in R (8/24/2026) \# response code \# \# Example if columns are shuffled \# library(dplyr) \# df_B \<- df_B %\>% \# rename(col1 = slight_diff_name1, col2 = slight_diff_name2) %\>% \# select(colnames(df_A))

Use library(waldo) to find missing subfields

```{r}
subfields_df <- subfields_df |> 
  mutate(Subfield = subfield_name)

library(waldo)

subfields_df_A <- subfields_df$Subfield
subfields_df_B <- alex_doi_new1$Subfield

# Elements in A that are completely missing from B
unshown_subfields <- setdiff(subfields_df_A, subfields_df_B)
```

response modified to be shown as a table

```{r}
unknown_subfields <- subfields_df |> 
  filter(Subfield %in% unshown_subfields)

```
